title: data.pdf — section 296
text:
(2) Where a witness who is required to attend before the Crown Court by virtue
of a witness summons fails to attend in compliance with the summons, the
Crown Court may—
(a) in any case, cause to be served on him a notice requiring him to
attend the court forthwith or at such time as may be specified in the
notice;
(b) if the court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing
that he has failed to attend without just excuse, or if he has failed to
comply with a notice under paragraph (a), issue a warrant to arrest
him and bring him before the court.

(3) A witness brought before the Crown Court in pursuance of a warrant under
this section may be remanded by that court in custody or on bail (with or
without sureties) until such time as the court may appoint for receiving his
evidence or dealing with him under section 51G.
